jobs.prompt: TOP PRIORITY bug (atlas-seafloor has 5 blockers from it): swarm integrate leaves the verified output uncommitted. (1) The orchestrator then needs a hand-build approval just to commit swarm-produced files, and (2) the dirty checkout blocks every later integrate and the autopilot (tools/autopilot.mjs line ~380 refuses with the checkout has uncommitted changes). Fix: after the integration succeeds and the merge-queue checks pass, integrate commits the run's own output itself on the swarm branch. No hand-build request is needed. Where: integrateRunLocked in tools/swarm.mjs (line ~1472) for plain integrate and the queue path (the final step of integrate --queue, which lives in the tools/swarm/ modules; find the function that finishes a queue integration and records state.integratedFiles and integratedHashes), reusing commitOutputs from tools/go.mjs (it stages exactly the given files with git add -- and commits; never git add -A). Rules (all must hold, otherwise NO commit and a one-line reason is printed and recorded): (a) only when the branch checked out in the integrated root is a swarm branch: its short name starts with swarm/ (git symbolic-ref --short HEAD); never on main, master, release branches, HEAD detached, or any other branch (current behavior unchanged there); (b) only after the checks passed (a failed or rolled-back integration commits nothing, exactly as today); (c) only the run's own integrated files (state.integratedFiles, plus integratedNewFiles) are staged, by explicit path; (d) before staging, the index must contain no other staged file (git diff --cached --name-only is empty): otherwise skip with the reason other files are already staged, never mix; (e) each integrated file's current content hash must equal the recorded integratedHashes entry (a file edited by hand after integration is left out and the whole commit is skipped with the reason naming it); (f) a file that is not changed relative to HEAD after the run (nothing to commit) is not an error; (g) generated state files (coordination/HANDOFF.md, docs/state/usage-ledger.md, coordination/TASK.md) and .swarm are never staged by this commit even if listed; (h) the commit message is: swarm integrate: run RUNID (T-0001, T-0002): N files, a blank line, then one line per file path, then the lines Swarm-Run: RUNID and Swarm-Tickets: IDS (ticket ids come from the manifest jobs: job.ticket, or a job id of the form T- followed by digits; omit the parenthesis and the tickets line when the run has no ticket); the author is the git configured user, never an invented address, and no Co-Authored-By line; (i) retry git commit up to 3 times with 300 ms pauses when .git/index.lock exists; (j) the commit is made with the same git environment the rest of integrate uses (no hooks bypass flag; the repository hooks run normally; a hook refusal is reported as the reason and leaves the files staged for a clean retry: unstage them with git restore --staged on failure so the tree is not left half-staged). (k) the integrate result JSON gets a commit object: { status: committed | skipped | failed, sha, branch, files, message, reason } and the human output prints one line: committed N files on BRANCH: SHA8 (run RUNID) or committed nothing: REASON; the run state records it (state.integrationCommit) and a journal or Events line is appended (no owner approval record, no hand-build log entry: this is the swarm committing its own verified output). Opt-out and double-commit protection: the flag swarm integrate --no-commit and the option autoCommit: false disable it; the go flows that already commit their own wave or run output through commitOutputs (go with a manifest, go --scope waves, scale, ship, init: the wrappers at tools/swarm.mjs lines ~2482, ~2698, ~3847, ~3862, ~3893) must pass autoCommit false so their existing commits and messages are unchanged and nothing is committed twice. Add the flag to the integrate usage text and the command metadata (tools/watch-command-meta.mjs, tools/completion.mjs) so tests/completion.test.mjs still passes. Autopilot: tools/autopilot.mjs checkout dirty test (line ~380) must ignore the generated state files above (they change on every swarm command) so they alone never block an integrate, but any other dirty file still blocks with the existing message; the integrate step of the autopilot passes no --no-commit. Tests in tests/integrate-autocommit.test.mjs, hermetic (temp git repos, git with explicit user config and no signing, explicit environment, no ambient environment, no network, injected fakes for the worker run as the existing integrate tests do): on branch swarm/x a verified run is committed by integrate with the message naming the run and the ticket, only the run files are in the commit, the tree is clean afterwards and a second integrate of a new run works (the original blocker); the same on the queue path; on main, on a feature branch, and on a detached HEAD nothing is committed and the reason is printed; a failed check commits nothing and the files are put back as today; another staged file in the index makes it skip with the reason and the staged file stays staged; a hand-edited integrated file (hash mismatch) is left out and the commit is skipped with that file named; generated state files dirty in the tree are not swept in; --no-commit and autoCommit false skip it; go flows do not double commit (one commit, the existing message); a failing pre-commit hook leaves nothing staged and reports the reason; index.lock retry; the commit object in the result JSON and the journal line; the autopilot checkout check passes with only generated state files dirty and blocks with any other dirty file; the author is the configured git user. Keep every existing test passing (integrate, queue, go, autopilot, completion tests). No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: tests that reference swarm.mjs in passing are covered by the full suite run before merge.
